acceptance: Red test first: a boundary whose sync-main merges a policy.json with a key that only the merged code reads completes: the code index refresh and every later step parse the policy with the rebuilt binary, or the refresh runs after the rebuild step.
A policy key that no reader of the merged tree knows still fails the boundary with its name.
Docs in STE: the boundary steps doc records the order.
fix: The wave-149 boundary stopped at step 4: sync-main merged PR #1236, which added the policy key workflow.builder_selfcheck together with its reader, then refreshed the code index with the pre-merge binary, whose strict policy loader refused the unknown key. The rebuild is step 11. Move the code index refresh after the rebuild, or have sync-main rebuild before any step that parses the merged policy, so a reader and its key can land in one PR.
notes: Console route: boundary steps. Recovered by hand: make -C go build, reset-sha, rerun wave next.

summary: A PR that adds a policy key with its reader stops the next boundary, because sync-main parses the merged policy with the old binary before the rebuild step.
title: The boundary parses the merged policy with the rebuilt binary
